title: SSRI/SNRI antidepressant medicines: small increased risk of postpartum haemorrhage when used in the month before delivery
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: Drug Safety Update volume 14, issue 6, January 2021: 5
funder: not stated; a safety communication of the UK medicines regulator
result: Published 7 January 2021. SSRIs and SNRIs increase bleeding risk, thought to be through a serotonergic effect impairing platelet aggregation. After an EU review (PRAC, September to October 2020) of observational studies, use in the month before delivery was estimated to increase the risk of postpartum haemorrhage by less than two-fold; background rates in Europe in one study were 12.7% for blood loss over 500 mL and 2.8% over 1000 mL; severity was not reported, and no fatalities were flagged in the European dataset. The review found sufficient evidence to update the product information for citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline, desvenlafaxine, milnacipran, venlafaxine and vortioxetine, and the MHRA stated that warnings were being added. The update restates the association with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn and neonatal withdrawal and toxicity reactions.
